Incorporating SLOOS insights:
- Bank credit supply: The SLOOS reported a broad-based net tightening of lending standards in Q3 2020 across C&I (for firms of all sizes), CRE, and consumer credit (credit cards and auto), with some tightening in residential mortgages as well. Banks also cited weaker loan demand in several categories and anticipated further tightening for certain segments.
- Transmission implications: While the FOMC stance is highly accommodative (zero rates, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases, and outcome-based guidance), tighter bank standards and softer demand suggest a drag on the flow of credit through the banking channel—particularly for SMEs and CRE—dampening the effectiveness of accommodative financial conditions noted in the FSR.
- Net tone: Policy remains clearly dovish, but SLOOS evidence of constrained credit supply and softer demand tilts the balance toward greater caution on the outlook than the FSR alone would imply.

Adjusted assessment: slightly more negative overall than previously indicated.
